1.t: By the (angels) who tear out (the souls of the wicked) with violence;

2.t: By those who gently draw out (the souls of the blessed);

3.t: And by those who glide along (on errands of mercy),

4.t: Then press forward as in a race,

5.t: Then arrange to do (the Commands of their Lord),

6.t: One Day everything that can be in commotion will be in violent commotion,

8.t: Hearts that Day will be in agitation;

9.t: Cast down will be (their owners') eyes.

10.t: They say (now): "What! shall we indeed be returned to (our) former state?

11.t: "What! - when we shall have become rotten bones?"

12.t: They say: "It would, in that case, be a return with loss!"

13.t: But verily, it will be but a single (Compelling) Cry,

14.t: When, behold, they will be in the (full) awakening (to Judgment).

15.t: Has the story of Moses reached thee?

16.t: Behold, thy Lord did call to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa:-

17.t: "Go thou to Pharaoh for he has indeed transgressed all bounds:

18.t: "And say to him, 'Wouldst thou that thou shouldst be purified (from sin)?-

19.t: "'And that I guide thee to thy Lord, so thou shouldst fear Him?'"

20.t: Then did (Moses) show him the Great Sign.

22.t: Further, he turned his back, striving hard (against Allah).

23.t: Then he collected (his men) and made a proclamation,

24.t: Saying, "I am your Lord, Most High".

25.t: But Allah did punish him, (and made an) example of him, - in the Hereafter, as in this life.

26.t: Verily in this is an instructive warning for whosoever feareth (Allah).

27.t: What! Are ye the more difficult to create or the heaven (above)? (Allah) hath constructed it:

28.t: On high hath He raised its canopy, and He hath given it order and perfection.

29.t: Its night doth He endow with darkness, and its splendour doth He bring out (with light).

30.t: And the earth, moreover, hath He extended (to a wide expanse);

31.t: He draweth out therefrom its moisture and its pasture;

32.t: And the mountains hath He firmly fixed;-

33.t: For use and convenience to you and your cattle.

34.t: Therefore, when there comes the great, overwhelming (Event),-

35.t: The Day when man shall remember (all) that he strove for,

36.t: And Hell-Fire shall be placed in full view for (all) to see,-

37.t: Then, for such as had transgressed all bounds,

38.t: And had preferred the life of this world,

40.t: And for such as had entertained the fear of standing before their Lord's (tribunal) and had restrained (their) soul from lower desires,

41.t: Their abode will be the Garden.

42.t: They ask thee about the Hour,-'When will be its appointed time?

43.t: Wherein art thou (concerned) with the declaration thereof?

44.t: With thy Lord in the Limit fixed therefor.

45.t: Thou art but a Warner for such as fear it.

46.t: The Day they see it, (It will be) as if they had tarried but a single evening, or (at most till) the following morn!
